metadata._verificationNotes: 75 curated entries focused on large, sustainable, recurring volunteer programs with national or chapter-based footprints. Each entry has a real _source URL. Local/ephemeral programs are NOT in this DB by design — they are surfaced via the on-demand /api/volunteer/discover-local endpoint.
metadata.description: Curated database of large, sustainable, recurring volunteer programs. The Wayfinder volunteer module also offers an on-demand "discover local" feature that uses live web search to find programs not in this DB.

opportunities.name: Hospital Junior Volunteer Program
opportunities.description: Junior volunteer programs at hospitals offer high-school students 14-18 the chance to work directly in patient care areas (with supervision), administrative support, gift shops, way-finding, and family lounges. Excellent for pre-med students. Most require ~50-100 hours/year minimum. Application typically opens in spring; selection is competitive at top hospitals.
opportunities.howToStart: Search "{your hospital name} junior volunteer program" — most hospitals have an online application opening February-April. Background check, TB test, and orientation required.

opportunities.name: American Red Cross Volunteer
opportunities.description: Multiple roles for teens 14+: blood drive support, disaster shelter staffing, Red Cross Youth clubs, international humanitarian advocacy, and CPR/First Aid instruction. Disaster response roles open at 18. Excellent training program; nationally recognized credential.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit redcross.org/volunteer to find local chapter opportunities by zip code. Some roles require 18+; most teen roles start in school chapters or summer camps.

opportunities.name: Special Olympics Volunteer / Unified Partner
opportunities.description: Volunteer at local Special Olympics events as a coach, Unified Partner (athlete partnered with a Special Olympics athlete), event staff, or fundraiser. Year-round at chapter level. Unified Champion Schools program is school-based, easier entry point.
opportunities.howToStart: Find your state chapter at specialolympics.org. School-based Unified Champion Schools programs are the easiest entry — talk to your school athletics director.

opportunities.name: Ronald McDonald House Charities Volunteer
opportunities.description: Help families with children receiving medical treatment by serving meals, doing light housekeeping, organizing activities, or fundraising. 365+ houses across the US. Most accept volunteers 14+, some 12+ with parent.
opportunities.howToStart: Find local house at rmhc.org. Most have monthly Meals from the Heart programs your family or club can sign up for.

opportunities.name: Crisis Text Line
opportunities.description: Trained volunteer crisis counselors respond to texts from people in mental health crisis. Requires intensive 30-hour training. **Must be 18+.** One of the most respected mental health volunteer credentials. 4-hour weekly shift commitment for one year minimum.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply at crisistextline.org/become-a-volunteer. Application includes references, background check, and ~30 hours of training before shifts begin.

opportunities.name: Public Library Teen Volunteer
opportunities.description: Most public libraries have structured teen volunteer programs: shelving, summer reading program assistance, tech help for seniors, story time helpers, craft program leaders. Reliable weekly hours, friendly staff, low entry barrier.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit your local library website or ask at the reference desk. Most run summer programs (May-August) requiring a brief application.

opportunities.name: Khan Academy Peer Tutor
opportunities.description: Peer tutoring program where students help younger learners through Khan Academy content. School-based clubs (Khan Academy Club) coordinate this. Flexible, free, scalable to any subject area.
opportunities.howToStart: Check if your school has a Khan Academy Club. If not, propose one to a teacher and use Khan's school onboarding materials at khanacademy.org/khan-for-educators.

opportunities.name: Reading Partners
opportunities.description: One-on-one literacy tutoring for K-4 students who need extra help. Available in 10+ states (CA, NY, MD, NC, SC, TX, WA, CO, OK, MN). 12-week commitment, 45-minute sessions twice weekly. Strong evidence base of impact.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit readingpartners.org and select your region. Background check + 1 training session required before tutoring begins.

opportunities.name: 826 National Writing Tutor
opportunities.description: Writing tutoring and creative writing workshops for under-resourced students K-12. Centers in Boston, Brooklyn, Chicago, Detroit, LA, NYC, Mid-Manhattan, Minneapolis, San Francisco, Washington DC, Tulsa. Founded by Dave Eggers. Strong literary community.
opportunities.howToStart: 826national.org has a chapter locator. Each chapter has its own application process; expect a writing sample.

opportunities.name: Big Brothers Big Sisters Volunteer (Bigs/Beyond School)
opportunities.organization: Big Brothers Big Sisters of America
opportunities.description: One-to-one youth mentoring. School-based (Bigs in School) opens to teens 14+; community-based mentorship typically requires 18+. Multi-year commitment expected. National network with chapters everywhere.
opportunities.howToStart: Use bbbs.org chapter finder. Bigs in School (high school students mentoring elementary kids) is the teen-accessible track at most chapters.

opportunities.name: School-Based Peer Tutoring (NHS / Beta Club)
opportunities.description: Most high schools have peer tutoring programs through National Honor Society, Beta Club, or subject-specific honor societies (Mu Alpha Theta for math, Tri-M for music, etc.). Reliable weekly hours, easy to start, well-recognized.
opportunities.howToStart: Talk to your school's counseling office or NHS faculty advisor. Most programs run September-May with weekly tutoring blocks.

opportunities.name: National Park Service Volunteers-In-Parks (VIP)
opportunities.description: Volunteer at any of 400+ national park sites: trail maintenance, visitor center staffing, junior ranger program leadership, citizen science projects, archaeology digs. Some sites have residential programs for high-schoolers in summer (Student Conservation Association partnerships).
opportunities.howToStart: volunteer.gov is the official portal — search by location and skill. SCA (thesca.org) runs residential summer programs for youth.

opportunities.name: Sierra Club Local Outings & Conservation
opportunities.description: Local chapters (60+ across the country) run volunteer days: trail building, restoration projects, advocacy training, conservation education. Some chapters have ICO (Inspiring Connections Outdoors) — leading youth on outdoor experiences.
opportunities.howToStart: Find local chapter at sierraclub.org/chapters. Check their events calendar for the next volunteer workday.

opportunities.name: Audubon Society Citizen Science (Christmas Bird Count, Climate Watch)
opportunities.description: The longest-running citizen science project (Christmas Bird Count) has 80,000+ annual volunteers. Year-round bird counts and habitat surveys. Local Audubon chapters also run habitat restoration and education programs.
opportunities.howToStart: audubon.org/volunteer to find local chapter. Christmas Bird Count happens Dec 14 - Jan 5 annually.

opportunities.name: Local Watershed / Stream Cleanup
opportunities.description: Most metro areas have a watershed council or "Friends of [River/Lake]" group running monthly cleanups, water quality monitoring, and restoration plantings. Easy entry, family-friendly, visible impact.
opportunities.howToStart: Search "Friends of [your local river or lake]" or check American Rivers (americanrivers.org) for local affiliates.

opportunities.name: Earthwatch Teen Expeditions
opportunities.description: Field research expeditions led by scientists; teen-specific programs in marine biology, climate change, archaeology, wildlife. 10-14 day intensive programs. Costs $2,000-3,500 plus airfare; need-based aid available. Major credential for science-focused students.
opportunities.howToStart: earthwatch.org/expeditions/teen — apply 6-8 months in advance. Need-based scholarships available.

opportunities.name: Student Conservation Association (SCA)
opportunities.description: Largest provider of conservation service opportunities for youth. High School Crews (4-5 weeks summer) and Conservation Internships (3-12 months gap year). Stipends + housing + AmeriCorps Education Award for longer programs.
opportunities.howToStart: thesca.org — High School Crew applications open November for summer programs. Highly competitive at flagship parks; less so at lesser-known sites.

opportunities.name: Local Humane Society / SPCA Volunteer
opportunities.description: Animal shelters always need volunteers: dog walking, cat socialization, foster home support, adoption events, kennel cleaning. Most shelters accept teens 14+ (some 12+ with parent). Year-round, very low barrier to entry.
opportunities.howToStart: Search "[your city] humane society volunteer" — orientation typically required. Younger volunteers often start with cat socialization or laundry/cleaning before moving to dog walking.

opportunities.name: Wildlife Rehabilitation Center Volunteer
opportunities.description: Wildlife rehab centers care for injured/orphaned wild animals. Volunteer roles: feeding orphaned birds, cage cleaning, education program assistance, transport drivers. Higher animal-handling responsibility comes with training. State licensing requirements vary.
opportunities.howToStart: Find state rehabbers via your state Department of Fish & Wildlife. Most run spring volunteer drives before baby season (April-July).

opportunities.name: Best Friends Animal Society (Local Chapters + Sanctuary)
opportunities.description: No-kill animal welfare org with chapters in NY, LA, Atlanta, Salt Lake City, Houston, Northwest Arkansas. Volunteer at adoption centers, foster, transport. The Utah sanctuary takes teen volunteers for week-long stays.
opportunities.howToStart: bestfriends.org/get-involved — local chapter or sanctuary stays available.

opportunities.name: Local Food Bank (Feeding America Network)
opportunities.description: 200+ food banks across the country. Volunteer roles: sorting donations, packing emergency food boxes, distribution events, mobile pantries. High-impact, very high frequency need. Easy for groups, families, or individuals.
opportunities.howToStart: feedingamerica.org/find-your-local-foodbank — every food bank has a volunteer page. Many run weekly Saturday morning sort events.

opportunities.name: Soup Kitchen / Community Meal Program
opportunities.description: Most communities have soup kitchens or community meal programs (often church- or shelter-based) that serve hot meals daily/weekly. Roles: meal prep, serving, cleanup, dishwashing. Usually requires only one orientation shift.
opportunities.howToStart: Search "[your city] soup kitchen volunteer" — Salvation Army, Catholic Charities, and local churches typically operate them.

opportunities.name: Meals on Wheels
opportunities.description: Deliver hot meals to homebound seniors. Drivers must be 18+ with valid license; passengers/ride-alongs accepted at 14+. Most programs need 1-2 hour weekday lunch shifts. Brief, high-impact human contact for isolated seniors.
opportunities.howToStart: mealsonwheelsamerica.org — find local provider. School-based MoW clubs exist in some areas; check your guidance office.

opportunities.name: Community Garden Volunteer
opportunities.description: Community gardens grow produce for local food pantries while teaching urban agriculture. Most cities have multiple sites. Plant, weed, harvest, deliver. Minimal weekly commitment, friendly community.
opportunities.howToStart: communitygarden.org garden finder. Most parks departments also list community gardens on their websites.

opportunities.name: Habitat for Humanity (Build Sites + ReStore)
opportunities.description: Build affordable housing alongside future homeowners (build sites: typically 16+) or work the ReStore (donated home goods retail; 14+). 1,400+ US affiliates. Iconic high-school service experience.
opportunities.howToStart: habitat.org/volunteer — find local affiliate. Build sites need 16+; ReStore takes 14+. Group days easy to organize for clubs/sports teams.

opportunities.name: Salvation Army Local Volunteer
opportunities.description: Year-round programs at 7,500+ US centers: food pantries, holiday red kettle bell-ringing (November-December), thrift stores, homeless shelters, after-school programs. Easy entry, lots of hour-flexibility.
opportunities.howToStart: salvationarmyusa.org — find local Corps. Bell-ringing November-December is the easiest entry; they'll take any willing volunteer.

opportunities.name: Family Promise Volunteer
opportunities.description: Helps homeless families with children. 200+ affiliates across the country. Volunteers prepare meals, set up sleeping rooms in host congregations, provide childcare during meetings, drive families to appointments.
opportunities.howToStart: familypromise.org affiliate finder. Most affiliates need volunteers for evening meal-and-host shifts.

opportunities.name: Nursing Home / Assisted Living Visitor
opportunities.description: Direct one-on-one or group visits with isolated elders. Activities: reading, music, games, technology help, conversation. Programs often coordinate through facility activity directors. Schools and faith communities often organize regular visits.
opportunities.howToStart: Call the activity director at any local nursing home / assisted living. Most welcome individual volunteers and especially repeat visitors who form ongoing relationships.

opportunities.name: AARP Volunteer (Tax-Aide, Driver Safety)
opportunities.description: AARP's Tax-Aide is the largest volunteer-run free tax prep program (must be 18+ for IRS-certified roles, but high school helpers can do greeting and reception). Driver Safety also has youth-supported roles.
opportunities.howToStart: aarp.org/volunteer — Tax-Aide season runs January-April; training in November-December.

opportunities.name: NAMI (National Alliance on Mental Illness) Volunteer
opportunities.description: 600+ local affiliates run support groups, education programs (Family-to-Family, Ending the Silence in schools), and walk fundraisers (NAMIWalks). Teen volunteers can lead Ending the Silence presentations after training.
opportunities.howToStart: nami.org/find-your-local-nami — Ending the Silence is school-based and trains teen presenters.

opportunities.name: Letters Against Isolation
opportunities.description: Write letters to seniors in care facilities. Fully remote, flexible, accessible to any age. Provides specific seniors and prompts. Low intensity but meaningful for chronically isolated elders.
opportunities.howToStart: lettersagainstisolation.com — sign up, get assigned a senior, mail a letter. No background check needed.

opportunities.name: Color a Smile
opportunities.description: Color drawings/cards that get distributed to seniors, deployed military, and others who need cheering up. Lowest-barrier remote service — works for elementary kids through adults. Good entry point for service-shy younger teens.
opportunities.howToStart: colorasmile.org — download printable templates, color, mail to their PO box.

opportunities.name: Best Buddies Chapter Member
opportunities.description: School- and community-based one-on-one friendships between people with and without intellectual/developmental disabilities. Strong school chapters; expect 1-2 hours/month minimum with assigned buddy. National jobs program also has volunteer mentors.
opportunities.howToStart: bestbuddies.org — check if your school has a chapter; if not, you can start one with their school onboarding kit.

opportunities.name: Therapeutic Riding / Equine-Assisted Programs
opportunities.description: Therapeutic horseback riding for individuals with disabilities. Volunteers serve as side-walkers, horse leaders, barn assistants. PATH International has 800+ certified centers. Typically requires 14+ and a one-time training session.
opportunities.howToStart: pathintl.org has a center finder. Most centers run lessons Tuesday-Saturday with consistent volunteer slots.

opportunities.name: Election Day Poll Worker (16+ in many states)
opportunities.description: 40+ states now allow 16- or 17-year-olds to serve as poll workers (paid, often $150-300/day). Set up the polling location, check in voters, distribute ballots, count machines. High-impact civic experience.
opportunities.howToStart: Check your state's Secretary of State website (or eac.gov for federal coordination). Apply in fall for November elections; primaries are also available.

opportunities.name: Court Appointed Special Advocate (CASA) — Limited Teen Roles
opportunities.description: Trained volunteers advocate for abused/neglected children in court. Most CASA roles require 21+, but several state CASA programs have Teen Advocates or Mentors for older youth in foster care (typically 18+ with training).
opportunities.howToStart: nationalcasagal.org/find-a-program — for high schoolers, ask your local CASA about Teen Advocate or admin support roles.

opportunities.name: Town Council / School Board Youth Representative
opportunities.description: Many municipalities have Youth Advisory Councils or non-voting student reps on school boards. Direct exposure to local policy-making. Strong leadership / policy interest signal.
opportunities.howToStart: Email your school board secretary or town council clerk. Some applications open spring for September terms.

opportunities.name: Museum Docent / Educator (Junior Tracks)
opportunities.description: Many museums have junior docent programs for high school students: gallery interpretation, leading school group tours, hands-on activity facilitation. Multi-year commitment expected at top-tier museums (Met, MFA Boston, Smithsonian); typically requires 80+ hours of training.
opportunities.howToStart: Email education departments at your top 1-3 local museums. Junior docent application typically opens spring, training summer, tours start fall.

opportunities.name: Theatre Volunteer (Box Office, Ushering, Set Crew)
opportunities.description: Regional theatres and community theatres always need ushers, box office, set construction, costume help. Great way to support arts and meet creative people. Free shows often included as a perk.
opportunities.howToStart: Email your local community theatre directly. Most have ongoing usher rotations.

opportunities.name: UNICEF UNITES (US Fund for UNICEF)
opportunities.description: School and community clubs supporting UNICEF's global child welfare work. Trick-or-Treat for UNICEF, advocacy campaigns, fundraising, awareness events. School chapters easy to start.
opportunities.howToStart: unicefusa.org/teens — start a UNICEF Club at your school or join an existing one.

opportunities.name: Translators Without Borders Volunteer (Bilingual Required)
opportunities.description: Translate humanitarian content for crisis-affected communities. Fully remote. Requires near-native fluency in source + target language. Excellent for bilingual students; meaningful global service entry.
opportunities.howToStart: translatorswithoutborders.org/volunteer — application requires language proof and 18+. Some sister orgs accept younger translators.

opportunities.name: Community Emergency Response Team (CERT)
opportunities.description: FEMA-sponsored neighborhood emergency response training. Teen CERT programs in many cities for 14+. 20+ hours of disaster preparedness, light search/rescue, fire safety, first aid. Recognized credential.
opportunities.howToStart: ready.gov/cert — find local CERT program through your city's emergency management office.

opportunities.name: Key Club International (Kiwanis Youth)
opportunities.description: High school service club chartered through Kiwanis. 250,000+ members in 5,000+ schools globally. Annual service projects (March of Dimes, Children's Miracle Network), local community service, leadership development. Convention/conference circuit.
opportunities.howToStart: keyclub.org — check if your school has a chapter, or ask the office about chartering one.

opportunities.name: Rotary Interact Club
opportunities.description: High school service club chartered by local Rotary Club. Two service projects annually (one community, one international). Strong adult mentorship, networking with local business community, scholarship pipeline.
opportunities.howToStart: rotary.org/interact — find your local Rotary Club via their site; they sponsor school chapters.

opportunities.name: Girl Scouts Gold Award / Boy Scouts Eagle Project
opportunities.description: Capstone service projects: 80-100 hours of independent leadership on a community-focused project. Eagle Scout and Gold Award are widely recognized credentials with measurable college admissions value.
opportunities.howToStart: Active Scouts: talk to your troop leader about Eagle/Gold timeline. Non-Scouts: must join a troop first; many regions have flexible older-teen tracks.

opportunities.name: Seattle Children's Hospital Junior Volunteer
opportunities.description: Top-rated children's hospital with a competitive junior volunteer program for high-schoolers 16+. Roles: family resource center, gift shop, surgical waiting area, child life support. ~100-hour annual minimum.
opportunities.howToStart: seattlechildrens.org/about/volunteering — applications open March-April for fall. Background check + immunization records.

opportunities.name: Northwest Harvest Volunteer
opportunities.description: WA's leading food bank network. Volunteer at Kent SODO warehouse (Seattle area) or one of 375+ partner food banks. Group-friendly, year-round shifts.
opportunities.howToStart: northwestharvest.org — sign up for Saturday morning sort shifts in Kent or partner pantries throughout WA.

opportunities.name: Mary's Place (Family Shelters, WA)
opportunities.description: Seattle-based family shelter network. Teen volunteers (14+) help with kids' programs, meal service, donation sorting. Family-friendly entry point.
opportunities.howToStart: marysplaceseattle.org/volunteer — group-friendly shifts at multiple locations.

opportunities.name: Woodland Park Zoo Junior Zookeeper / Teen Volunteer
opportunities.description: Seattle zoo's teen programs: Junior Zookeeper (summer, paid stipend, competitive), ZooCorps year-round, ZooU education volunteers. Strong conservation/biology track.
opportunities.howToStart: zoo.org/teens — Junior Zookeeper applications open January for summer.

opportunities.name: YMCA Y Service Squad
opportunities.description: YMCA branches run teen volunteer corps for camp counseling, swim lessons, after-school programs, fundraisers. 2,700+ Y locations nationally. Easy to scale to leadership roles. Many Y's are also CPR-training certified.
opportunities.howToStart: ymca.net to find local Y. Most have year-round teen volunteer rosters.

opportunities.name: Boys & Girls Clubs of America Volunteer
opportunities.description: 4,800+ clubs serving 4M+ kids annually. Teen volunteers help with after-school homework, sports, arts, tech programs. Easy entry, family-friendly schedules.
opportunities.howToStart: bgca.org/find-a-club — local club volunteer coordinator handles application.

opportunities.name: Make-A-Wish Foundation Volunteer
opportunities.description: Granting wishes to children with critical illnesses. Most direct wish-granter roles require 21+, but teens can volunteer for special events, fundraisers, office support, transportation logistics.
opportunities.howToStart: wish.org — contact local chapter; teen-appropriate roles vary by chapter.

opportunities.name: Hospice Volunteer (Family Companion / Vigil)
opportunities.organization: National Hospice and Palliative Care Organization affiliates
opportunities.description: Sit with terminally ill patients and their families. Most programs require 18+ and 30+ hours of training. Profound experience; strong signal of emotional maturity. Some hospices have teen tracks for non-clinical support.
opportunities.howToStart: nhpco.org find a hospice — apply to local hospice; expect 30 hours of training and background check.

opportunities.name: Habitat ReStore (Donated Goods Retail)
opportunities.description: ReStore is Habitat's home-improvement thrift store funding builds. Teen volunteers (14+) work donations intake, retail floor, organizing, deliveries. Lower-barrier than build sites.
opportunities.howToStart: habitat.org/restores — find local ReStore.

opportunities.name: American Cancer Society Relay For Life / Teen Programs
opportunities.description: Major fundraising events (Relay For Life, Making Strides Against Breast Cancer), school-based DetermiNation, hope lodge volunteer support. Teen leaders run school relay teams.
opportunities.howToStart: cancer.org/involved — search Relay For Life by zip code or start a school team.

opportunities.name: American Heart Association School Volunteer
opportunities.description: School-based fundraising (Kids Heart Challenge, Hoops For Heart), community CPR training events, patient support. AHA-certified CPR instruction is a strong skill credential.
opportunities.howToStart: heart.org/volunteer — local affiliate has youth/school programs.

opportunities.name: Doctors Without Borders Student Ambassador
opportunities.description: Student-led MSF Student Coalition chapters at 50+ universities, with high school feeder events. Awareness campaigns, fundraising, advocacy on global health crises. Strong med-school pipeline signal.
opportunities.howToStart: doctorswithoutborders.org/get-involved — student coalition resources for school chapters.

opportunities.name: Salvation Army Bell Ringer (Holiday Season)
opportunities.description: Iconic Red Kettle bell-ringing November-December. Easiest entry point to large-scale service. 2-hour shifts, no application required for most stores.
opportunities.howToStart: registertoring.com — sign up for 2-hour shifts at a local store November-December.

opportunities.name: Local Hospital Pet Therapy Visit (Therapy Dog International)
opportunities.description: Trained dog + handler teams visit hospitals, nursing homes, schools, libraries. Requires the dog be evaluated and certified through TDI or Pet Partners. Family-friendly with parent handler.
opportunities.howToStart: tdi-dog.org or petpartners.org — evaluation requires several months of training.

opportunities.name: Habitat for Humanity Global Village (International Build Trips)
opportunities.description: 1-2 week international build trips. Costs $1,500-3,500 plus airfare. Highly structured, safety-conscious. Limited slots for 16-17 year olds (must travel with parent/guardian).
opportunities.howToStart: habitat.org/volunteer/travel-build/global-village — applications 4-6 months in advance.

opportunities.name: Voter Registration Drive Volunteer
opportunities.organization: Various nonpartisan groups (League of Women Voters, Rock the Vote, When We All Vote)
opportunities.description: Help register new voters at schools, festivals, community events. League of Women Voters runs high-school chapters in many states. Nonpartisan civic engagement.
opportunities.howToStart: lwv.org/local-leagues or whenweallvote.org. Many high schools allow drives during senior class meetings.

opportunities.name: Goodwill Industries Volunteer
opportunities.description: Goodwill stores, donation processing, career resource centers. Less prestige than some, but very high accessibility and frequent shifts.
opportunities.howToStart: goodwill.org/locator — local Goodwill volunteer coordinator.

opportunities.name: Local Election Day Driver / Polling Site Setup
opportunities.description: Help set up polling locations early morning, drive voters who lack transportation, deliver ballots between sites. 16+ in many states. Paid in some jurisdictions.
opportunities.howToStart: County elections office — apply 6-8 weeks before election day.

opportunities.name: Local Library Tech Coach for Seniors
opportunities.description: Teach seniors basic smartphone, email, video chat, online safety. Most libraries have weekly digital literacy hours. High satisfaction from both sides.
opportunities.howToStart: Ask at your library reference desk — most have ongoing digital literacy programs needing volunteers.

opportunities.name: Junior Achievement Volunteer (Classroom Mentor)
opportunities.description: Bring financial literacy and entrepreneurship lessons into K-12 classrooms. Volunteers (typically 18+, but teen helpers in some chapters) deliver pre-built curriculum. Local-business-heavy.
opportunities.howToStart: ja.org/volunteer — match with local school based on your background.

opportunities.name: RIF (Reading Is Fundamental) Book Drive Captain
opportunities.description: Run book drives at school or in community to provide books to kids in low-income areas. Strong project-based leadership opportunity. RIF supplies organizing materials.
opportunities.howToStart: rif.org — get the book drive starter kit and organize at your school.

opportunities.name: Operation Warm (Coat Drive)
opportunities.description: Annual coat collection and distribution to children in need. School-based coat drives easy to organize as a sophomore/junior leadership project.
opportunities.howToStart: operationwarm.org — partner with a local school or shelter for distribution.

opportunities.name: Parks Department Trail Maintenance Crew
opportunities.description: Most state and county parks departments run weekend trail maintenance crews. Physical work, outdoor, family-friendly. State Parks Foundations often recruit teens.
opportunities.howToStart: Search "[your state] State Parks volunteer" or "[your county] parks volunteer".

opportunities.name: Local Synagogue/Church/Mosque/Temple Service Programs
opportunities.description: Most faith communities run multiple service projects: meal prep for shelters, after-school tutoring, holiday baskets, immigrant support, addiction recovery support, eldercare visits. Open to non-members in most cases.
opportunities.howToStart: Email the social action / outreach committee chair at a local congregation.

opportunities.name: Local Suicide Prevention Walk Volunteer (AFSP)
opportunities.description: Out of the Darkness Walks happen in 600+ cities each fall. Volunteer roles: registration, route marshal, family lounge, post-walk reception. Powerful entry point to mental health advocacy.
opportunities.howToStart: afsp.org/walks — find walk near you, sign up to volunteer.

opportunities.name: Tax-Aide IRS-Certified Volunteer Preparer
opportunities.description: Free tax preparation for low-income filers. Requires IRS certification (~30 hours of training, exam). Must be 18+. Excellent quantitative skills credential.
opportunities.howToStart: aarpfoundation.org/taxaide — November-December training for January-April season.

opportunities.name: Free Clinic Volunteer (Translators, Reception, Logistics)
opportunities.description: Free/low-cost clinics need bilingual translators, intake clerks, supply organizers. Spanish-English translators highly valued. Excellent pre-med exposure without clinical role.
opportunities.howToStart: Search "free clinic [your city]" or freeclinics.com for the National Association of Free & Charitable Clinics.

opportunities.name: AmeriCorps Service Year (Post-HS, Gap Year)
opportunities.description: Year-long full-time service ($30K+ stipend + $7K education award). Programs: City Year, Teach For America Corps Member, NCCC. Must be 17+. Major gap year option for committed service-oriented students.
opportunities.howToStart: americorps.gov/serve — applications 3-6 months ahead of service year start.

opportunities.name: UNICEF Volunteer Translation / Content Review (Remote)
opportunities.description: UN Volunteers Online has remote volunteer opportunities in translation, content review, web design, research, training material development. International credential, fully remote.
opportunities.howToStart: onlinevolunteering.org/en — must be 18+ and create a profile.

opportunities.name: Community Bike Repair Coop
opportunities.description: Community bike co-ops fix bikes for low-income community members and teach repair skills. Practical hands-on skills, environmental angle, transportation equity. Most metros have one.
opportunities.howToStart: Search "[your city] bike kitchen" or "community bike co-op".

opportunities.name: FareStart Volunteer (Kitchen, Events, Job-Skills Support)
opportunities.description: Seattle-based job-training nonprofit (founded 1992) that uses food-service training to lift people out of poverty and homelessness. Volunteers provide kitchen support for prepared-meals programs, conduct practice interviews with adult and youth students, distribute fresh produce from partner farms, and help with events and office work.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply via the Volunteer page at farestart.org/volunteer or email volunteer@farestart.org. Most shifts are at FareStart's Seattle locations; minors typically need a parent/guardian co-shift.

opportunities.name: Discovery Corps (Pacific Science Center)
opportunities.description: Year-round youth-development program at Seattle's Pacific Science Center for area high-schoolers. Members start as floor-volunteer interpreters demonstrating exhibits to museum guests and after about 100 service-learning hours can advance to paid interpreter and intern roles. Program intentionally recruits students underrepresented in STEM.
opportunities.howToStart: Visit pacificsciencecenter.org/about/careers and look for the Discovery Corps youth opening, or contact Pacific Science Center's youth programs team. Cohort recruitment is typically annual.

opportunities.name: Seattle Humane — Humane Teen Club & High School Service Shifts
opportunities.description: Two volunteer pathways for teens at Seattle Humane (Bellevue, WA). The Humane Teen Club (ages 13-17) meets two Saturdays per month during the school year to learn shelter operations and animal-welfare topics; graduates are eligible for select volunteer roles including summer opportunities. High School Service Shifts let students entering grades 9-12 earn community-service hours by washing food/water bowls, cleaning transfer crates, and packing pet food.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply for the Humane Teen Club or High School Service Shifts at seattlehumane.org/get-involved/youth-school-programs/youth-programs or email EducationServices@seattlehumane.org. Programs run at 13212 SE Eastgate Way, Bellevue (small registration fee for Service Shifts).

opportunities.name: EarthCorps Volunteer Restoration Events
opportunities.description: EarthCorps runs habitat-restoration volunteer events year-round across the Salish Sea region — Seattle, Burien, Tukwila, Tacoma, and Everett — engaging roughly 10,000 youth and community volunteers per year. Tasks include removing invasive English Ivy and Himalayan Blackberry, planting native trees and shrubs, and spreading mulch. Open to all ages; volunteers under 14 must be accompanied by an adult.
opportunities.howToStart: Browse upcoming restoration events at earthcorps.org/volunteer and register online. Events are typically Saturday mornings; tools and gloves are provided.

opportunities.name: Treehouse for Kids — Volunteer & Treehouse Store
opportunities.description: Treehouse (founded 1988) is the only Washington nonprofit focused exclusively on the educational, material, and financial needs of youth in foster care, serving more than 7,000 youth across the state each year. Volunteer roles include sorting donations and assisting at the Treehouse Store in Seattle (which provides free clothing and school supplies to foster youth) and supporting events. Shifts are open to youth age 12 and older; volunteers age 16+ can volunteer on their own.
opportunities.howToStart: Sign up via treehouseforkids.org/take-action/volunteer or email volunteer@treehouseforkids.org to be added to the waitlist. Treehouse Store is at 2100 24th Ave S, Seattle.

opportunities.name: Hopelink Volunteer (Eastside / North & East King County)
opportunities.description: Largest non-profit in north and east King County since 1971, operating food markets, weekly community dinners, gleaning, food rescue, and home delivery for low-income clients across Bellevue, Kirkland, Redmond, Shoreline and Sno-Valley. In 2025 over 2,000 volunteers donated 61,730 hours. Volunteer roles include warehouse sorting, market shopping support, weekly Avondale Park dinners, gleaning at local farms, and home delivery.
opportunities.howToStart: Submit the online volunteer application at hopelink.org/ways-to-help/volunteer/, complete a Washington State Patrol background check, then attend a virtual New Volunteer Orientation. Minimum age 16; some roles 18+. Group volunteering also available.

opportunities.name: Seattle Aquarium Youth Ocean Advocates (YOA)
opportunities.description: Teen volunteer and advocacy program running continuously since 1994, with over 2,500 alumni and ~140 active teen volunteers from across the Puget Sound region. Two tiers: YOA Tides (newsletter + monthly digital meet-ups, open to any high school-aged person) and YOA Currents (hands-on interpreters at the Aquarium with access to behind-the-scenes trainings, marine science classes, and policy advocacy including Olympia Lobby Day for plastics legislation).
opportunities.howToStart: Submit interest form at seattleaquarium.org/act-for-the-ocean/volunteer/youth-ocean-advocates/. Summer cohort interest opens in January; school-year cohort opens in May. Applicants must be in grades 9-12 (high school, Running Start, GED, or homeschool). Attend an info session, then complete an application and interview. Currents tier requires a minimum of 8 volunteer activities (3-5 hours each).

opportunities.name: KCLS Teen Volunteer Program (TVP) & Teen Advisory Boards
opportunities.description: Teen-led KCLS program operating since June 2020 across King County's library network (50+ branches including Bellevue, Redmond, Issaquah, Kent, Auburn, Federal Way). The Teen Volunteer Program empowers teens to plan, create, and lead online and in-branch events and workshops for kids, teens, and families — earning community service hours and leadership experience. Teen Advisory Boards meet regularly with a librarian facilitator to co-design library programming. Branch-level teen volunteer roles are available at most KCLS locations.
opportunities.howToStart: Fill out the TVP Interest Form at kcls.org/news/teen-volunteer-program-tvp/ or contact a teen services librarian at any branch. Teen Advisory Boards are also available at most branches. Most Teen Advisory Boards are open to high schoolers; some accept middle schoolers. Volunteers logging 10+ hours in 6 months may request reference letters.

opportunities.name: Washington Trails Association Volunteer Trail Work Parties
opportunities.description: Largest state-based hiking advocacy and trail-stewardship organization in the U.S., founded in 1966. WTA's volunteer trail crews log 100,000+ hours per year repairing and maintaining hundreds of miles of public trails across Washington — Mount Rainier, North Cascades, Olympic peninsula, Issaquah Alps, Tiger Mountain, Capitol Forest, and dozens more. Single-day work parties, week-long Backcountry Response Teams, and Youth Volunteer Vacations.
opportunities.howToStart: Browse and register for a work party at wta.org/volunteer. Volunteers must be 10+; under 14 must be accompanied by a registered adult, and all under-18 volunteers must be signed in by a parent or guardian. Wear sturdy closed-toe shoes and long pants — bring your own lunch. WTA provides tools, training, and a free day-use pass.

opportunities.name: Point Defiance Zoo & Aquarium Youth Volunteer Program (Zoo Guides)
opportunities.organization: Point Defiance Zoo & Aquarium (Metro Parks Tacoma)
opportunities.description: Youth volunteer corps at one of the oldest combined zoo-and-aquarium facilities in the U.S. (founded 1905). High school Zoo Guides educate visitors about wildlife, conservation, and Pacific Northwest ecosystems through interpretive carts, animal-encounter stations, and programs across the Asian Forest Sanctuary, Rocky Shores, Pacific Seas Aquarium, and Wild Wonders Outdoor Theater. Additional youth-eligible roles: Spot the Swallows (Feb, 14+ with parental supervision) and Explore the Shore (16+).
opportunities.howToStart: Zoo Guide applications open December and require a 1-year commitment for youth ages 14-18 in grades 9-12. Apply at pdza.org/connect/volunteer (Youth Volunteering page). Background check is required for all volunteers 18+; under-18 require a parent-signed permission form. Located at 5400 N. Pearl St., Tacoma.

opportunities.name: Tacoma Rescue Mission Volunteer (Kitchen, Mentoring, High Impact)
opportunities.description: Pacific Northwest's largest emergency-services and recovery mission for people experiencing homelessness, founded in 1912. Three daily kitchen shifts every day of the year, plus Women's Shelter assistance, Donation Center sorting, landscaping, retail at Mission Thrift, and the Good Neighbor Village volunteer program. "High Impact" volunteers (6-month minimum, 18+) mentor clients, tutor youth/adults, and assist case workers and Search & Rescue street outreach.
opportunities.howToStart: Create a volunteer account at rescue-mission.volunteerhub.com. Minimum age is 8 (children 8-13 must volunteer with an adult; under-18 require a Youth Waiver). Donation Center and Litter Pick-Up roles require age 18. For deeper impact, apply to a High Impact role at trm.org/highimpact (interview + 6-month commitment). Closed-toe shoes and long pants required.

opportunities.name: Second Harvest Inland Northwest Volunteer (Sort, Pack, Teaching Kitchen)
opportunities.description: Eastern Washington and North Idaho's lead Feeding America food bank, distributing tens of millions of pounds of food each year to a 26-county service area from its Spokane and Pasco distribution centers. Volunteers sort and repack donated food, fill backpack-program kits (Bite2Go) for kids, support mobile markets, prep meals in the Kitchen at Second Harvest culinary-training kitchen, and staff Child Hunger Center events.
opportunities.howToStart: Register and book shifts at volunteer.2-harvest.org. Anyone 14+ may volunteer independently; ages 9-13 must be accompanied by a parent or adult chaperone (no children under 9). Spokane Volunteer Center is at 1234 E. Front Ave; a Pasco location also hosts shifts. Teen-friendly later shifts are available after school during winter months.

opportunities.name: Greentrike / Children's Museum of Tacoma Volunteer
opportunities.description: Tacoma's nonprofit play-based learning organization operating the Children's Museum of Tacoma, the Children's Museum at JBLM, the Monarch Diaper Bank, Play to Learn, and other early-learning programs across Pierce County since 1985. Volunteer roles include leading Early Learning Activities with museum visitors during 2-hour shifts, packaging diapers for the Monarch Diaper Bank, prepping art and STEAM materials, and supporting special events such as the Right to Play Gala.
opportunities.howToStart: Submit the Online Volunteer Contact and Application Form at greentrike.org/about/volunteer. Ongoing volunteers must be at least 14 (with a 14-17 parent/guardian permission form) and pass a background check. Registration through the Volunteer Management Information System (VMIS) is required. Children's Museum of Tacoma is at 1501 Pacific Ave.

opportunities.name: Mobius Discovery Center Volunteer (Spokane)
opportunities.description: Spokane's hands-on STEAM children's museum (formerly Mobius Children's Museum), serving more than 100,000 visitors per year in downtown Spokane and through outreach to Eastern Washington elementary schools. Volunteers staff the exhibit floor, prep supplies for hands-on arts, crafts, and simple science activities, assist with class visits, and support special programs. Shifts run flexibly at the museum (331 N. Post St.) and at partner schools.
opportunities.howToStart: Volunteers must be at least 16 (15 and under may volunteer alongside an adult 18+) and pass a criminal background check. Apply via the volunteer page at mobiusdiscoverycenter.org/join/volunteer or contact Volunteer Manager Alina Morrisey at amorrisey@mobiusspokane.org.

opportunities.name: Renewal Food Bank Volunteer (Bellevue / East King County)
opportunities.description: East King County food bank founded in 1998 (formerly Bellevue LifeSpring Food Bank), serving more than 500,000 individuals to date. Volunteer roles include sorting and stocking, packing grocery bags for home delivery, transporting donations from grocery partners, organizing neighborhood food drives, and team-building volunteer days.
opportunities.howToStart: Sign up via the Volunteer page on renewalfoodbank.org. Choose individual, group, or team-building shifts (one-time, bi-monthly, or weekly). Volunteers ages 14+ may serve on their own; under 14 may volunteer during non-operational hours with an adult chaperone. Court-ordered community service is also accepted.

opportunities.name: The Sophia Way Volunteer (Bellevue / Eastside Women's Shelters)
opportunities.description: Eastside-based homelessness services for adult women. Operates Sophia's Place day and overnight shelter in Bellevue and Helen's Place in Kirkland. Volunteer roles include the Donation Center (sorting/organizing donated goods), Shelter Assistance (women only, planning and hosting events for guests), the Youth Engagement Committee for high school students focused on advocacy and fundraising, and special events.
opportunities.howToStart: Register at sophiaway.org/volunteer. Donation Center in Bellevue (Wednesdays 12-2pm) accepts volunteers 16+ on their own; ages 10-15 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian. Shelter Assistance is restricted to women 18+ (13-17 with parent). High schoolers can apply to the Youth Engagement Committee for ongoing advocacy work.

opportunities.name: KidVantage Volunteer (formerly Eastside Baby Corner)
opportunities.description: Pacific Northwest nonprofit (formerly Eastside Baby Corner, founded 1989) providing clothing, baby supplies, diapers, and essential goods to children of families in need. Operates four hubs (Issaquah, Shoreline, Bremerton, plus mobile drop-offs across the Puget Sound region). Volunteer tasks include sorting and packaging clothing/diapers/baby goods, intake and inventory at hubs, and community drive organizing.
opportunities.howToStart: Sign up via kidvantagenw.org/volunteer. Welcomes volunteers ages 12 and up; volunteers ages 12 and 13 must be accompanied one-to-one by an adult. Group opportunities available — contact the volunteer coordinator listed on the page.

opportunities.name: Eastside Friends of Seniors Volunteer
opportunities.description: Sammamish-based nonprofit partnering with the East King County community to help older adults live independently and stay socially connected. Volunteer roles include transportation (to medical appointments, grocery shopping, essential services), friendly visiting, household help, technology assistance, and special events. Drivers are particularly needed.
opportunities.howToStart: Sign up at eastsidefriendsofseniors.org/volunteer. All volunteers must be 16+ (drivers 21+). Commitment is at least 2-5 hours of service per month for 6 months. Choose your activity and schedule from the Volunteer Opportunities list.

opportunities.name: LifeWire Volunteer (Eastside Domestic Violence Services)
opportunities.description: Bellevue-based largest comprehensive domestic violence service provider in Washington State. 40 years of operations serving 148,000+ survivors and their children. Volunteer roles include Stewardship Ambassador (donor thank-you calls/cards), Event Assistant (planning and operating fundraising events such as the World of Hope Gala), Social Media Content Strategist, in-kind donation drive hosting (diaper, baby-supply, birthday-party kits), Community Advocacy outreach, and the 20-hour Domestic Violence 101 training pathway for direct survivor-support roles.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply via the volunteer form at lifewire.org/get-involved/volunteer/. Volunteers under 18 must be supervised by a parent or guardian and may not be eligible for all opportunities. LifeWire offers at least one 20-hour DV 101 training per year for advocacy roles.

opportunities.name: Share Vancouver Volunteer (Hot Meals, Backpack, Shelter, Garden)
opportunities.description: Vancouver WA's largest hunger-relief and homelessness-services nonprofit, founded 1979. Operates the Share House emergency shelter system, Hot Meals daily community dining, Backpack Program (food bags for students/families weekly during the school year), Talkin' Trash environmental advocacy, Care for Share fundraisers, and the Share Garden/produce program. Volunteer roles span kitchen prep, meal serving, dishwashing, food sorting/packing, garden maintenance, donation processing, and community events.
opportunities.howToStart: Create a profile at sharevancouver.org/volunteer and complete the volunteer application + background check. Volunteers must be at least 16 to volunteer independently; under-16 must be accompanied by an adult. Some programs (Hot Meals at Share House) are Ages 18+ or group-only; the Backpack and Garden programs accept Ages 12+ as part of a 5-10 person group.

opportunities.name: Clark County TeenTalk Peer Volunteer Program
opportunities.organization: Clark County TeenTalk (Clark County Community Services)
opportunities.description: Teen-to-teen confidential support program in Clark County, WA. TeenTalkers answer calls, texts, and emails from peers facing issues like family conflict, depression, anxiety, school stress, identity, abuse, and crisis. Volunteers complete a structured 32-hour pre-service training (active listening, suicide-risk basics, community resources, role plays) before being paired with adult mentor coordinators on the line. Hybrid: in-person and Zoom shifts available. Hours count toward senior project and community service credit.
opportunities.howToStart: Apply via the Google Form linked at ccteentalk.clark.wa.gov/get-involved-teens.html. Eligible: youth ages 15-19 living in Clark County. Commit to 32 hours of pre-service training plus one supervised 3-hour shift per week. Contact program coordinator at 564-397-5199.

opportunities.name: Capitol Land Trust Stewardship Work Parties
opportunities.description: Tumwater-based regional land trust conserving wildlife habitat, working farms/forests, and shorelines across Thurston, Mason, Lewis, Grays Harbor, and Pacific counties. Stewardship work parties run year-round at conserved preserves and easements (Bayshore, Stephens, Black River, Darlin Creek, and many more). Activities include planting native trees and shrubs, mulching, removing invasive species like Scotch broom and Himalayan blackberry, trail maintenance, and debris cleanup. K-12 outdoor programs and Salmon Docent / Trail Steward roles also available.
opportunities.howToStart: RSVP to upcoming work parties at capitollandtrust.org/get-involved/stewardship-work-parties/ or subscribe to The Heron newsletter. Minors under 16 must be accompanied by an adult and have a Minor Waiver Release form signed by a parent or guardian. Contact stewardship@capitollandtrust.org with questions.

opportunities.name: City of Vancouver Urban Forestry / Friends of Trees Tree Planting
opportunities.organization: City of Vancouver Urban Forestry (with Friends of Trees)
opportunities.description: Vancouver WA's official urban tree-canopy program, run by City Public Works in partnership with Friends of Trees (1+ million native trees and plants put in the ground across Portland-Vancouver since 1989). Tree planting season runs October through April with neighborhood plantings nearly every weekend; Friends of Trees provides gloves, tools, and on-site training, and neighborhood volunteers host a community potluck after each planting. Year-round Stewardship Saturdays focus on watering, mulching, and weeding established trees.
opportunities.howToStart: Sign up for individual planting events at friendsoftrees.org or via the City of Vancouver Urban Forestry events calendar. Youth 15 and under must volunteer with a parent or guardian; youth 16+ may volunteer independently with a parent-signed youth waiver form. For Vancouver planting questions, email AdelaM@friendsoftrees.org or call 360-487-8308.

opportunities.name: Thurston County Food Bank Volunteer (Olympia, Lacey, Tumwater)
opportunities.description: South Sound's largest hunger-relief organization, serving Thurston County since 1972. Operates the Olympia Food Pantry, Lacey Food Pantry + Farm Stand, Tumwater Warehouse, Mobile Food Bank, Food Rescue, agricultural programs, and Backpack Program for school-age kids. Volunteer roles include client-services pantry shifts (greeting clients, packing food orders, restocking), warehouse sort/repack, farm stand setup, food rescue driving, and special events. M-F daytime shifts plus the 2nd Wednesday of each month evening shift in Lacey and select Saturday Farm Stand mornings.
opportunities.howToStart: Complete the online volunteer application at tcfb.org/volunteer/volunteer-basics/ then sign up for shifts via the VolunteerLocal portal. Youth ages 12+ may volunteer without parental supervision; under 12 must be accompanied by an adult; under 18 require a parent/guardian signature on the application. Court-referred community service accepted.
